newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge sees '97 nickel output rising. [CORRECTED 16:24 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge sees '97 nickel output rising. [CORRECTED 16:24 GMT]

text.p: Falconbridge Ltd chief executive Oyvind Hushovd said on Friday the company is forecasting nickel production to rise to about 100,000 tonnes in 1997 from 92,000 tonnes in 1996.
Falconbridge also expected to spend between C$950 million and C$1.0 billion (corrects from C$1.0 million) on capital expenditures in 1997, Hushovd told reporters after the company's annual meeting.

Hushovd said he expected Falconbridge's Sudbury operations to produce between 67,000 and 68,000 tonnes of nickel in 1997. Falcondo, the company's operation in the Dominican Republic, is forecast to produce up to 31,000 tonnes.
"All and all, that should keep us pretty close to 100,000 tonnes (in 1997)," Hushovd told reporters.
He said nickel production costs are expected to trend downward in 1997.
"If you look to the cost we had in the first quarter, I think we might have lower costs in the quarters to come," Hushovd said.
During the meeting, Hushvold told shareholders the year is off to a good start. "Our production has remained strong and operating costs are trending down," he said.
Falconbridge reported net income of C$46.1 million, or C$0.26 per share, in the three months ended March 31.
Earnings were 66 percent higher than the fourth quarter of 1996, but down from C$72.4 million, or C$0.41 per share, in the first quarter of 1996.
Weaker operating income and revenues in the first quarter of 1997 reflected lower average realized prices for nickel, copper and cobalt.
Falconbridge reported an average realized nickel price of US$3.50 per pound in the first quarter, down from US$3.81 per pound in the first quarter of 1996.
The average price for ferronickel fell to US$3.32 per pound in the first quarter from US$3.66 per pound in the same period for 1996.

First quarter copper prices dipped to US$1.12 per pound from US$1.18 per pound in prior year. Zinc prices rose to US$0.57 per pound in the first quarter from US$0.52 per pound in the first quarter of 1996.
